clue.text: Fail to comprehend performance that's sweet

definitions.note: a noun here: a sugar, something sweet

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in, so the word for failing holds the performance inside it

parts.note: to fail is to lose
a performance is an act

explanation.surface: Someone who misses the point of a show that everyone else found charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk sugar is a sweet substance, so the sugar found in milk counts as a sweet in the noun sense.

clue.text: I'm surprised a soldier lifted a Native American

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

explanation.surface: Surprise as a paratrooper raises a Native American aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Plains people of the American West, so one of them is a Native American.

clue.text: Greek letter something to pick up, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the phrase is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to pick up the tab is to pay the bill, so the thing picked up is the tab

explanation.surface: A Greek character that is easy to learn, put tersely.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet, used for angles in mathematics.

clue.text: See 13
Worst possible thing where one deals with a breakdown

definitions.meaning: slang for anything dreadful, the very bottom

definitions.text: where one deals with a breakdown
definitions.meaning: in motor racing the pit lane area is where a broken-down car gets repaired

explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls something awful the bottom of everything, and racing teams fix failing cars in the trackside garages of that name.

clue.text: See 13
Mediocre earner needing sink and kettle, say?

parts.note: to pot a ball in snooker is to sink it
a kettle is an example of something that boils water

explanation.surface: A kitchen fitting job: a sink and a kettle wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or film churned out for money, of little quality, is an inferior earner.

clue.text: Cultivation shown by jailbird in hat

indicators.note: in means the jailbird is placed inside the hat word

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
an old lag is a habitual prisoner

explanation.surface: A prisoner wearing a hat shows refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughing and preparing land for crops is cultivation of the soil.

clue.text: Totally perplexed, when all humour has drained away?

definitions.meaning: utterly baffled, not knowing what to do

definitions.text: when all humour has drained away?
definitions.meaning: read literally, the point at which one's jokes and cleverness have run out

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means baffled and desperate, while taken literally it describes the end of one's supply of clever humour.

clue.text: See 24
Last of the rubbish written about vehicle taken back, as claws drawn in

indicators.note: taken back means the whole assembled string is read in reverse order
the last letter of the word that follows is used
the word for rubbish is written around the vehicle, enclosing it

parts.note: rubbish dropped in the street is litter
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A report on a car being repossessed, with a stray mention of cats' claws.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus LIT(CAR)TER gives ELITCARTER, and 'taken back' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats can pull their claws back in, and the adjective describes body parts able to be withdrawn like that.

clue.text: Land bordering a western country

indicators.note: one country bordering letters means it sits around them on both sides

parts.note: Mali is a West African country

explanation.surface: A land that shares a frontier with some western nation.
explanation.definitionFit: This southeast African state is a land, a country, in the geographical sense.

clue.text: I've no cash, and I threaten all in need of treatment?

definitions.text: I've no cash, and I threaten all in need of treatment?

indicators.note: letters in need of treatment get worked on and reshaped, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped public body warning that it can no longer care for the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's state-funded healthcare system; the whole clue is it complaining of its underfunding, and the fodder skips 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's free public medical system treats patients and is perpetually short of funds, which the whole clue voices.

clue.text: Direction turned another way

indicators.note: turned means twisted around into a new arrangement

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: An instruction to face somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a compass point, halfway between two cardinal points, so a direction to head in.

clue.text: Message on the box, switch hit and power terminated

indicators.note: to switch is to swap things around, so these letters change order

parts.note: sway is power or influence
up means finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: Instructions for flicking a switch, hitting something and cutting the power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' seems to be a TV, but it is a packing case.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipping cartons are printed with this instruction so they are kept upright.

clue.text: Rapid group at sea

definitions.meaning: a body of ships sailing together, a navy squadron

explanation.definitionFit: The word means swift as an adjective and also names a navy's collection of ships as a noun.

clue.text: Add ten, providing nothing rejected

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: providing means if
FA is short for 'sweet FA', slang for nothing at all
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Put in ten more, as long as none is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach or append something is to add it, as in fixing a stamp to an envelope.

clue.text: Nowhere near end of disorder, back in confusing mess

parts.note: far means nowhere near

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: ago means back in time, as in years back

explanation.surface: Disorder is far from over and it is back to chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumbled hotchpotch of ideas or things is a muddled, confused mixture.

clue.text: Brexit no deal initially unfolding, potentially volatile situation?

indicators.note: unfolding events develop and change shape, so the letters are rearranged
initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Political commentary: a no-deal Brexit playing out could be explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: A box of dry kindling catches fire at a spark, so figuratively it describes a situation ready to flare up.

clue.text: Figure going into another dip shortly, one covering one's face

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a visor is a face shield

explanation.surface: A masked person diving about while some number is divided.
explanation.definitionFit: In division, the number you divide by goes into the other number.

clue.text: Excessive land of Suleiman the Magnificent, for example?

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive
Oman is a land on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A grand sultan's realm is said to be overblown.
explanation.definitionFit: Suleiman the Magnificent was a sixteenth-century Turkish sultan, an example of a member of that empire's ruling dynasty.

clue.text: Result of lack of planning putting leader on edge

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: Theresa May was the UK Prime Minister, a national leader
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Poor planning that unsettles a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was the British Prime Minister at the time, struggling with Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos and disorder follow when nothing has been organised in advance.

clue.text: Murder squeezing in boozer — might these get you in?

indicators.note: the birds squeeze the pub in between them, enclosing it

parts.note: a murder is the collective noun for a group of crows
boozer is British slang for a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: A killing in a pub, then a question about gaining entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murder' looks like a crime but is the collective noun for those black birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglars force doors and windows open with these iron levers, so they could get you inside.

clue.text: A nasty vice being impudent — lippy here?

definitions.note: lippy is British slang for lipstick, kept in this kind of little bag

indicators.note: impudent behaviour is cheeky and out of order, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A cheeky, mouthy vice, with 'lippy' read as insolent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lippy' seems to mean cheeky, echoing 'impudent', but it is British slang for lipstick, which is stored in a make-up bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cosmetics bag carries lipstick and powder, so lipstick would be kept inside one.

clue.text: Hunter-gatherer possibly missing nuts?

parts.note: no means none, without
nuts means mad

explanation.surface: A forager perhaps lacking a supply of nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunter-gatherers usually wander from place to place, so one may be a wanderer with no fixed home.

clue.text: Queen, perhaps yet to snub English Oscar winner, cheers

parts.note: a queen is an example of a chess piece, a chessman

indicators.note: to snub is to ignore or leave out, so the English letter is dropped

parts.note: Tom Hanks won Academy Awards for Philadelphia and Forrest Gump

explanation.surface: The Queen has yet to cold-shoulder an English film star at an awards night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty or the band, but it is a piece in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: In British use 'cheers' is a casual thank-you, the same as an expression of great gratitude.

clue.text: Imitative behaviour has crossword writer doubled up

indicators.note: doubled means the piece appears twice in a row

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter, bent over laughing, is copying someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologist Richard Dawkins coined the term for a unit of culture passed on by imitation.

clue.text: Soft little things, the English to the Australians, one and all?

parts.words: the English to the Australians, one
parts.note: Australians call an English person a pom, so one of them is this
and all of them together are the plural, poms

explanation.surface: Australians' term for the English, used for every last one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: These are fluffy balls of wool or yarn, small soft decorations on hats and cheerleaders' hands.

clue.text: Naval weapon, flipping scandal, with inclination to waste billions

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over so it reads backwards

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

indicators.note: to waste the billions is to lose them, so the letter goes

parts.note: a bent is an inclination or leaning

explanation.surface: An outraged rant about a weapons programme wasting billions.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is also the name of the UK's submarine-launched nuclear missile system, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's sea-based nuclear deterrent bears this name, as does the three-pronged spear of the sea god Neptune.
